SceneManager._scene._actorWindow

SceneManager._scene._actorWindow.active

The easiest way to do this is to use the null chaining operator. This will only look at the property if it exists.
Note that
@rpgLord69
is correct - HUDMaker doesn't know how to do anything with an actor object, you need to be checking for which specific actor is being targeted and turn the appropriate HUD element on/off with that information.
So you make your graphic that's highlighting the first party member's portion of the HUD, and give it the eval
Code:
return SceneManager._scene._actorWindow?.active && SceneManager._scene._actorWindow?.index() == 0;
then make another one highlighting the second party member using a 1 at the end, etc.
